articles.summary: What does it take to build a career in tech sales at a biotech software company? Six women at Benchling share their paths, and the advice they'd give anyone coming up behind them.
articles.title: Women in Sales at Benchling

articles.summary: Benchling AI has helped scientists find and analyze data. Now Agents can act on it — registering molecules, running analyses, and flagging risks before they compound — all automatically as work happens. Here's what that means for R&D teams.
articles.title: Introducing Benchling Agents, your infinite program team

articles.summary: Benchling users can now run predictive AI models trained on decades of Eli Lilly's proprietary research data — flagging antibody developability issues and small molecule small molecule property prediction signals before a single assay is run.
articles.title: Lilly TuneLab pharma-powered AI models now in Benchling

articles.summary: Benchling published BenchBench-Protocol, a benchmark testing if LLMs can troubleshoot wet lab protocols like expert scientists. Top models still miss the practical judgment lab work requires, showing a real gap between knowing biology and doing it.
articles.title: Can LLMs work in the wet lab?

articles.summary: Benchling launches vibe coding: scientists can now prompt AI to build shareable, reproducible R&D applications like candidate dashboards and program trackers.
articles.title: Vibe coding enters the lab

articles.summary: Chemistry and biology R&D have long lived in separate tools. Benchling is changing that — introducing Chemistry Reactions for single-step synthesis planning and predictive ADMET models, all connected to the same scientific record.
articles.title: Benchling now brings chemistry and biology together
